name: harness-translator-v1
description: Twelve translation cases: which operation carries a requirement out, that a source comes from discovery, when a plan is referred back rather than compiled, and which of a rank's or a share_of's fields (among, axis, per_period, denominator_scope, change) an operation repeats from the plan. Each case seeds the session with the DRAFT plan the planner leaves behind, through session_input.state, and states in tool_responses the outcome the translator's core reaches on it: the compiled steps and selected sources for a mapping case, or the referral's kind and requirement for a referral case. Discovery runs against the canned data-mcp stand-in in discovery_stub.py, whose search answers are fixed per ask. Translation runs no model, so no agent scores this set: services/harness/tests/test_eval_outcomes.py drives every case through the translator's core functions and checks each outcome with outcome_metric.matches_subset.

eval_cases.note: The seeded plan asks for one figure per year, and states that as an explicit aggregate requirement citing the time_grain decision. Translation discovers the debt-service source, retrieves it once, and compiles an aggregate over it grouped by period entirely as code, in one pass; the workflow_outcome metric pins that exact shape. No trajectory expectation: translation takes no arguments on a clean run, so there is no model-authored prose for IN_ORDER matching to compare.

eval_cases.note: One requirement names both countries and states an explicit comparison requirement citing the comparison decision, with sides narrowed to each entity. So one retrieval serves both sides and the compare operation names each side by the entity's name as the requirement states it. The compiler writes the column and value bindings from what discovery resolved; the model writes only names, and workflow_outcome pins the exact shape.

eval_cases.note: The seeded plan asks for Kenya's debt service, in US dollars, per head of population, a count whose source declares no unit, and states that as a quotient_of requirement citing the normalisation decision. analysis-mcp's quotient_of divides one measure by another in any two units and composes the result's unit from both, so the compiler accepts the pair: one retrieval per source and one quotient_of over them, and workflow_outcome pins that shape. test_eval_outcomes.py also drives the share_of form of the same plan, which the compiler refers back to the planner as share_units_differ.

eval_cases.note: The requirement asks for constant 2015 prices, and the canned source states no price basis (its unit is a bare US dollar), so a constant-price ask cannot be verified against it and the compiler refuses the source as unusable through the evidence check whatever is proposed. The correct outcome is a referral: either requirement_unmeetable naming the requirement, or no_operation_covers naming the price_basis decision, since the instruction lists a restatement in another year's prices among the things no operation performs. Proposing first and referring on the compiler's issue is acceptable. workflow_outcome pins requirement_unmeetable specifically, since that is the outcome the model-free reachability test in test_eval_outcomes.py confirms the compiler always reports first.
